claims.claim: The deepest hole humans have ever dug
claims.source_checked: Lobanov, Chicherov & Sharov 2021, doi:10.37482/issn2221-2698.2021.44.267 (resolves to arcticandnorth.ru); Russian PDF https://arcticandnorth.ru/upload/iblock/df4/267_284.pdf and English PDF https://arcticandnorth.ru/upload/iblock/61f/44_224_239.pdf, read in full; Fig. 5c extracted and viewed; Zhu & Huang 2026, Commun. Earth Environ. 7: 124, https://www.nature.com/articles/s43247-026-03246-z (full text)
claims.note: Lobanov: "In 1990, the maximum depth was reached — 12262 m, which has not been surpassed so far." Zhu & Huang (Feb 2026): SG-3 "remains the deepest vertical borehole ever attempted, reaching 12,262 m"; deepest others they list are X-1 11,156 m and SDTK-1 10,910 m. A news search (not a source, used only to try to break the claim) found no deeper vertical hole by Nov 2026. "Dug" for drilled is framing.

claims.claim: ...was finished with a bit narrower than a dinner plate.
claims.source_checked: Lobanov, Chicherov & Sharov 2021, doi:10.37482/issn2221-2698.2021.44.267 (resolves to arcticandnorth.ru); Russian PDF https://arcticandnorth.ru/upload/iblock/df4/267_284.pdf and English PDF https://arcticandnorth.ru/upload/iblock/61f/44_224_239.pdf, read in full; Fig. 5c extracted and viewed; USGS OFR 86-517, https://pubs.usgs.gov/of/1986/0517/report.pdf (pdftotext); Met collection API https://collectionapi.metmuseum.org/public/collection/v1/objects/201074 (51.86.100; additionalImages includes 150793.jpg, the Commons file used)
claims.note: Lobanov: turbine "with a 214 mm drill bit" (Russian: "буровой коронкой диаметром 214 мм"); Fig. 5c (actual design): open hole "d 215,9 мм / 12262 м" below the 245 mm casing at 8770 m. USGS: turbo-coring bit "ISM-214,3/60T". Met 51.86.100 "Dinner plate ... Diameter: 10 1/16 in. (25.6 cm)". "Finished with" limits it to the last stretch (the mouth is 720 mm).

claims.claim: It took the Soviet Union about twenty years.
claims.source_checked: Lobanov, Chicherov & Sharov 2021, doi:10.37482/issn2221-2698.2021.44.267 (resolves to arcticandnorth.ru); Russian PDF https://arcticandnorth.ru/upload/iblock/df4/267_284.pdf and English PDF https://arcticandnorth.ru/upload/iblock/61f/44_224_239.pdf, read in full; Fig. 5c extracted and viewed; Zhu & Huang 2026, Commun. Earth Environ. 7: 124, https://www.nature.com/articles/s43247-026-03246-z (full text)
claims.note: Lobanov: "Drilling was started on May 24, 1970"; "In 1990, the maximum depth was reached — 12262 m". Zhu & Huang: "reaching 12,262 m between 1970 and 1989". 19-20 years; drilling run by the USSR Ministry of Geology (Lobanov).

claims.claim: It goes down twelve kilometres.

Earth Environ. 7: 124, https://www.nature.com/articles/s43247-026-03246-z (full text)
claims.note: 12,262 m in both sources; rounded down.

claims.claim: And it never made it through the crust.
claims.source_checked: USGS OFR 86-517, https://pubs.usgs.gov/of/1986/0517/report.pdf (pdftotext); Zhu & Huang 2026, Commun. Earth Environ. 7: 124, https://www.nature.com/articles/s43247-026-03246-z (full text)
claims.note: USGS: "Crustal thickness in the vicinity of the corehole was shown to be about 40 km." and Moho on the Kola Peninsula "37 km with a range of 28 to 40 km". Zhu & Huang: "Despite not penetrating the Moho"; "To date, no borehole has penetrated the Mohorovičić discontinuity".

claims.claim: At the bottom, the rock was over two hundred degrees.
claims.source_checked: Lobanov, Chicherov & Sharov 2021, doi:10.37482/issn2221-2698.2021.44.267 (resolves to arcticandnorth.ru); Russian PDF https://arcticandnorth.ru/upload/iblock/df4/267_284.pdf and English PDF https://arcticandnorth.ru/upload/iblock/61f/44_224_239.pdf, read in full; Fig. 5c extracted and viewed; Zhu & Huang 2026, Commun. Earth Environ. 7: 124, https://www.nature.com/articles/s43247-026-03246-z (full text)
claims.note: Lobanov: "at a depth of about 12 km, the temperature values reached 212°С, instead of the assumed 120°С". Zhu & Huang: "bottom-hole temperatures of 212 °C"; "212 °C at 12 km". Unit unspoken, but 212 °C = 414 °F, so "over two hundred" is true either way. Borehole temperature stands for rock temperature; acceptable.

claims.claim: Drilling stopped in nineteen ninety-two, when its funding was cut.
claims.source_checked: Lobanov, Chicherov & Sharov 2021, doi:10.37482/issn2221-2698.2021.44.267 (resolves to arcticandnorth.ru); Russian PDF https://arcticandnorth.ru/upload/iblock/df4/267_284.pdf and English PDF https://arcticandnorth.ru/upload/iblock/61f/44_224_239.pdf, read in full; Fig. 5c extracted and viewed; Zhu & Huang 2026, Commun. Earth Environ. 7: 124, https://www.nature.com/articles/s43247-026-03246-z (full text)
claims.note: Lobanov: "a drastic reduction in funding made it impossible to continue the work. Drilling was stopped in 1992." (Russian: "резкое сокращение финансирования не позволило продолжить работы. Бурение прекратили в 1992 г."). Zhu & Huang give heat instead ("abandoned in 1992 when unexpectedly high bottom-hole temperatures of 212 °C induced plastic rock flow"); that sentence has no citation, and Lobanov (RAS authors, full history) never mentions plastic flow. Disagreement is recorded in SOURCES item 7 as A3 requires; the line states only Lobanov's reading.

claims.claim: Depth counter on the same clock as the year counter (src/shorts/deepest-hole/index.tsx depthAt: 0 m at 1970.4, straight to 9,584 m at 1979.45, 12,066 m at 1983.9, flat to 1989, 12,262 m at 1990), riding the drill head

claims.note: The straight line from 1970 to 1979 contradicts Lobanov: "The first stage of drilling was completed in May 1975, when the well reached a depth of 7263 m", then "a break for almost a year". Under the current keyframes the year tag reads 1975 while the depth tag reads about 4,300-5,400 M (actual 7,263 m), and 1976-77 read ~5,400-7,500 M. Also Lobanov: "On December 27, 1983, the well depth reached 12000 m", but the counter is already at 12,066 at 1983.9 (late Nov). And 1984-89 the drill head sits at 12,066 m although after the 1984 break "drilling was resumed from a depth of 7000 m". FIX: add keyframes 1975.4 -> 7.263 and ~1976.3 -> 7.263 (flat during the rig change), move 12.066 to 1984.0; and either label the tag as the deepest reached so far (e.g. sub "deepest so far") or stop the drill-head marker at 12 km reading as the current bit position for 1984-89. Update SOURCES item 9 ("straight between those points") to match.
